counterfactual.change: No biomarker relaxation works: even all-comers (100%) predicts 282 months at 85 sites. The binding constraints are elsewhere — N=340 against 189 competing trials; feasibility would need ~510 sites even without the biomarker.

drivers: active disease thresholds (tender/swollen joint counts, elevated CRP/ESR) exclude many seropositive patients with low disease activity
requirement for inadequate response/stable dose on background DMARD/MTX therapy for defined duration excludes new or unstable patients
exclusion of prior biologic/TNF non-responders or any biologic use removes a substantial subset
restrictions on corticosteroid dose/timing and recent intra-articular/parenteral steroid use exclude additional patients
age and comorbidity exclusions (hepatic, renal, infection) further reduce eligible pool
eligibility.reasoning: Across precedent RA trials, the combination of strict active-disease thresholds (joint counts, CRP/ESR), required stable background DMARD/MTX therapy, and exclusion of prior biologic or TNF failures typically screens out a majority of otherwise biomarker-positive patients. Applying these compounded but partially overlapping filters to seropositive RA patients yields roughly a third passing all remaining inclusion/exclusion criteria.

failed_precedents.why_stopped: Business decision based on lack of enrollment
The biological effect seen with natalizumab was not sufficient to warrant further development in RA.

evidence.claim: Seropositive fraction of incident RA is 62% (37% dual RF+/anti-CCP+, 13% anti-CCP only, 12% RF only) in a population-based US cohort, 2003-2019, n=1373 -- the enrollable-population denominator for a seropositive-required trial.

input.mechanism: IRAK4 sits downstream of IL-1R/TLR-MyD88 signalling; small-molecule inhibition suppresses synovial fibroblast-driven and myeloid inflammatory output in RA.

why: 340 patients (effect size d=0.35) at 85 sites (p75 of at-scale precedents); precedent velocity 0.65 pt/site/mo across 196 completed trials (sampled from 2268 registered), narrowed by 62% biomarker prevalence and 35% eligibility pass rate, with ~189 interventional trials competing for the same patients.
